transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (NovaHealth CISO), Liam O'Reilly (IT Ops), Marisol Vega (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick check, is this still a 45 minute slot?
[00:12] Aisha: Yep that works. We wanted to keep it high level but also get into how you do SSO and SCIM because we have some compliance gating.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Agenda — quick intros, go over SSO/SAML set up, SCIM provisioning and group mapping, RBAC model, then demo or screenshots and next steps. Priya will drive the technicals.
[00:30] Priya: hi all, thanks. maybe start with SSO. NovaHealth, you mentioned you use Okta as your IDP, right?
[00:38] Aisha: Correct, Okta for enterprise, and Azure AD for a few teams. both need to be supported. we also require SAML certificate rotation every 90 days.
[00:48] Priya: we support Okta and Azure AD out of the box. Our SSO is SAML 2.0 compliant. For cert rotation, Redwood supports manual replacement and automated via metadata URL — we pull the IDP metadata and detect cert changes. There's also a window for JIT failover if a cert rotates unexpectedly.
[01:10] Liam: when you say JIT failover, do you maintain old certs for some time? we need to avoid a blast radius if something goes wrong.
[01:17] Priya: we keep the previous cert for a configurable grace period (default 7 days). admins can reduce it; we can also do zero-downtime rotation via dual-key acceptance while both active. it is configurable by the admin console or via API.
[01:33] Marisol: sounds good. how do you map groups from Okta to roles inside Redwood? our org uses groups for environment access.
[01:40] Priya: SCIM provisioning handles group sync. you can do either direct group-to-role mapping in our UI or push groups from Okta. we support group scoping and prefix matching. Example mapping: okta group "nh-platform-admins" -> Redwood Role "platform-admin". we can also map nested groups but there are caveats with some IDPs.
[02:05] Aisha: what SCIM attributes do you require? we have custom attributes (employeeType, costCenter) we want to flow.
[02:12] Priya: standard SCIM v2 attributes: userName, name, emails, groups, and we accept custom attributes in extension schemas. For costCenter we map extension urns. we'll send a sample mapping file after.
[02:25] Liam: provisioning cadence? near realtime?
[02:29] Priya: push from Okta is near real-time for create/update/delete. For large orgs we support bulk sync and delta sync. changes appear typically in under 30 seconds for push events.
[02:40] Jordan: quick qual — do you need SCIM disabled for some teams?
[02:45] Aisha: yes, we want SCIM for engineers but not for service accounts; we also want to restrict who can provision.
[02:50] Priya: you can scope SCIM to groups and enable SCIM on a per-application basis. we expose admin policies: who can manage users vs who can only assign roles.
[03:02] Marisol: on RBAC — what's your recommended least-privilege model for a company like us?
[03:07] Priya: recommend roles: org-admin (very limited), platform-admin, dev-lead, engineer, read-only/auditor. then apply resource-scoped roles for environment level (prod/staging). also use role inheritance sparingly. we recommend least-privilege by default and grant escalate via temporary elevation workflows.
[03:29] Aisha: temporary elevation — do you provide just-in-time elevate and audit?
[03:33] Priya: yes, we support time-limited role elevations with approvals and an audit trail. approvals can integrate with Slack/email and we log the reason and approver in the audit log.
[03:46] Liam: audit logs — retention and export? we have a SIEM that requires 12 months of logs.
[03:52] Priya: default retention is 90 days in console; longer retention is an add-on. we support forwarding logs to cloud destinations: S3, GCS, Azure Blob, or directly to SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. We can configure 12+ months retention and TTL in your own bucket if you need.
[04:12] Aisha: what about PII in logs? we need to ensure data minimization and masking.
[04:18] Priya: we mask user PII by default in console logs and our audit schema supports redaction. for forwarded logs to your storage, we can either forward raw or masked; by default we recommend masked, but we can provide raw for regulated auditing under an MDR process.
[04:34] Marisol: encryption at rest and in transit — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:39] Priya: Yes. Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest we support AES-256. For enterprise/private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys and HSM integration. For hosted, we offer an option for CMK via AWS KMS or BYOK on Dedicated. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[04:59] Aisha: good. data residency — we require EU data residency for NovaHealth EU entities. do you host logs and data in eu-west?
[05:07] Priya: we have region pins. For Hosted we support EU regions and you can pin the tenant to eu-west-1. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy to your VPC in eu-central or on-prem. We'll need to capture the exact project scope for the pilot.
[05:23] Liam: if we pin to eu region, what about KMS keys? can keys be in customer's account?
[05:28] Priya: yes, for Dedicated/Private you can manage keys in your own cloud account; for hosted we can enable CMK via a cross-account KMS key. documentation to follow.
[05:38] Jordan: Aisha, are there specific compliance docs you wanted today? SOC2, ISO?
[05:43] Aisha: SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certification evidence, plus our security questionnaire answers. also we want to review access controls mapping path for auditors.
[05:52] Jordan: we'll send SOC 2 and ISO docs, and Priya will fill the security questionnaire for the SCIM/SSO/RBAC parts.
[05:59] Priya: quick note on SAML assertions — you can configure assertion lifetime, audience, and encryption. we recommend shorter assertion lifetimes for sensitive apps. we also support MFA enforcement via IdP and post-auth checks.
[06:14] Marisol: do you allow attribute-based access, e.g., costCenter or dept attribute to gate resource access?
[06:20] Priya: we support attribute-based rules. You can create dynamic role assignments based on SCIM attributes, like employeeType=="contractor" => restricted role, costCenter tag for billing scoping.
[06:33] Liam: SCIM rate limits? we have 20k users.
[06:36] Priya: our SCIM endpoint handles enterprise scale; for very large orgs we'll set up bulk sync and higher rate limits via the dedicated plan. We'll need to know your user count to recommend config.
[06:48] Aisha: certificate/key rotation auditability — do you log who rotated keys and when?
[06:53] Priya: yes, all admin actions show actor, timestamp, IP, and change details in the audit log. exported logs include JSON fields for easy ingestion.
[07:03] Jordan: any networking constraints? Liam?
[07:06] Liam: IP allowlist for admin console and SAML endpoints, also SOCKS for legacy. we might require private peering for Dedicated.
[07:15] Priya: we support IP allowlists, SAML endpoints behind static IPs for Dedicated, and direct VPC peering for Private deployments. we can provide the list of egress IP ranges for hosted.
[07:25] Marisol: secrets management — how do you handle tokens and secrets?
[07:29] Priya: secrets are stored in an encrypted keystore, KMS wrapped. Rotation is supported via API; service tokens can be short lived and pinned to roles. For Dedicated/Private customers you can bring your own KMS.
[07:41] Aisha: auditors will ask about RBAC approvals and separation of duties. can you show role separation and enforced approvals?
[07:48] Priya: yes, our console shows role assignments and policy docs; approvals can be required for promotions or role assignments. we also provide reports for auditors that enumerate role histories.
[07:59] Jordan: i'm going to share a live doc link in chat with a sample SCIM mapping and the RBAC matrix.
[08:05] Aisha: perfect, we will take a look.
[08:09] Priya: demo note — i can show screenshots; full demo would be another session. is that ok?
[08:15] Marisol: screenshots fine for now. we need engineers to see the flow though before pilot.
[08:20] Priya: understood. screenshots: admin UI for SSO config, SCIM mapping UI, role mapping, and audit log view.
[08:29] Liam: logging destinations — do you allow push to our Azure storage?
[08:33] Priya: yes, Azure Blob supported. also direct Event Hub or Sentinel integration. we can set up an ingestion pipeline.
[08:41] Aisha: about sensitive data — do you perform any NLP on user data that could store PII? we need guarantees.
[08:48] Priya: default is no persistent storage of input data beyond what is required for inference and logging; for Hosted we have configurable retention and scrubbers and the option to disable any analytics that store raw inputs. For Private/Dedicated, all data stays in your environment if desired.
[09:02] Marisol: onboarding flow for pilot — can we try with 10 users and 2 groups first?
[09:07] Jordan: yes that's a common pilot. we'll scope it.
[09:10] Priya: action items recap coming, but quick technical Q: do you require SCIM push only or also read-only sync?
[09:17] Aisha: push is preferred but read is ok as backup.
[09:21] Priya: ok we'll recommend push with a periodic delta read.
[09:26] Jordan: quick callout — support for SAML encrypted assertions?
[09:29] Priya: supported, both signed and encrypted assertions. we can supply SP metadata you can upload to Okta.
[09:36] Liam: what about user sessions length and token revocation?
[09:40] Priya: session TTL configurable; admins can revoke sessions and invalidate tokens via API; SCIM deprovision triggers immediate session termination for that user.
[09:50] Marisol: we have a question on cross-account key access when using CMK. who has key access?
[09:56] Priya: for Hosted CMK, we do cross-account grants with least privilege. For Dedicated, keys live in your account and you control grants. We'll provide recommended IAM policies.
[10:10] Aisha: ok, good. any gaps you see for our compliance posture?
[10:14] Priya: from what you've said, main items: confirm EU residency pin, confirm SCIM attribute list and provisioning scope, confirm required retention for logs and whether auditors need raw logs. Once we have that we can propose pilot configuration and security docs.
[10:29] Jordan: we'll circle back with SOC2/ISO docs.
[10:33] Aisha: last question — do you support SCIM group deletions cascading to role removals? we need cleanups.
[10:38] Priya: yes, group deletions can cascade and trigger deprovisioning; you can enable soft-delete windows to avoid accidental removals.
[10:46] Jordan: time check, five minutes left, let's do quick recap and next steps.
[10:51] Priya: recap — Priya will share SCIM mapping and SSO setup guide; Jordan will send SOC2/ISO and security questionnaire; customer to confirm pilot users, EU residency, and IP allowlist.
[11:05] Aisha: that works. we'll review docs and get back.
[11:09] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and proposed times for the RBAC demo.
[11:14] Marisol: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription contains typical small errors; names may be mis-tagged in real export. Links referenced in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/security/sso-scim (example), sample RBAC matrix (shared in meeting chat).

End of transcript.
